trend.title: National Retail Vacancy Falls to 4.3% as Q3 2026 Absorption Hits Strongest Level Since 2023
trend.scope: U.S. retail real estate market, Colliers Q3 2026 national retail market statistics
trend.metric: 4.3% national retail vacancy (down 10 bps); 10.5 million sq ft net absorption, highest since 2023
trend.summary: Colliers reported that national retail vacancy declined 10 basis points to 4.3% in the third quarter of 2026, remaining near historic lows. Net absorption reached 10.5 million square feet, the highest quarterly total since 2023, driven by continued retailer expansion and the backfilling of available space. Shopping center vacancy improved to 5.4% and mall vacancy fell to 8.2%, while new construction remained constrained at 58.1 million square feet nationwide amid elevated construction and financing costs.
trend.significance: Retail vacancy near historic lows with limited new supply gives landlords more leverage in lease renewals and expansions, raising the stakes on co-tenancy, exclusive-use and percentage-rent clauses as tenants compete for scarce space. With construction pipelines constrained by financing costs, owners of well-located centers have fewer easy outs if a redevelopment or repositioning plan falls through, increasing the practical cost of disputes over lease terminations, assignment and tenant improvement allowances.
